chronology: [Recap] Steelhead receives the Medallion of High Nobility; Dona Vicenta publicly accuses him of killing her father, exterminating millions of Dylvaks, and destroying an ancient Halerce tree, then threatens suicide to deny him the honor.
[Recap] Steelhead tracks down Zaran Krleza—the last poet surviving as a 5,000-year-old disembodied head—and Endo-robots merge them into a new composite identity called Melmoth.
[Recap] Melmoth restores the Halerce tree on Philodendra and wins Dona Vicenta's love; when she realizes he is also her father's murderer, he offers her his life.

A woman (contextually Dona Vicenta) cannot shoot Melmoth and instead turns the gun on herself; mechanical observers link the event to Honorata reaching a temporal fissure point critical to Metabaron ancestry.
Melmoth deflects the bullet using Shabda-Oud psychic inheritance so his beloved is only stunned; he has her sent to the metabunker and searches Dona Vicenta's room for a crucial item.
A single living cell is recovered and a cloning operation is initiated; a humanoid body is progressively reconstructed inside a large incubation chamber.
The clone of Don Nicanor Rosamel de Rokha is declared complete; Dona Vicenta is awakened from a weeks-long coma and reacts with acute distress at her father's presence.

Melmoth reassures Dona Vicenta, confirms the father's return has drawn delegates from multiple planets toward the presidential palace, and warns a trial of socialization is still needed; the two exchange forgiveness and declarations of love, and Dona Vicenta promises him descendants.

Don Nicanor gives a triumphant ideological speech in a parliamentary chamber invoking Troglosocialik values and rejection of the Empire; Dona Vicenta recognizes his recovered memory and publicly embraces him as her father.

The clone shows memory instability: he fails to recognize Aina Vicenta Gabriela as his daughter, locks her in a private chamber, and makes inappropriate romantic advances; she insists her love is filial.
Melmoth forcibly embraces the woman and demands marriage; her white-haired father intervenes physically and restrains Melmoth; the woman pleads for both lives; Melmoth calls for guards.

The chamber comes under siege by loyalist forces who believe a mercenary is holding the president; attackers use a Paleo-Marx statue as a battering ram; the elder man proposes escape or lethal defense, but the president refuses either.

A speaker invokes Castaka doctrine and the imperative to produce a future Metabaron just before armed troops breach the chamber behind a caped leader; the framing narrative interrupts as Plea-Se pauses the story for dinner.
The next day inside the metabunker: Plea-Se refuses to continue the lineage recounting; Tonto declares the master is dead and will not return; Plea-Se insists on preparing a meal in case he returns.
Plea-Se seizes control of Tonto's programming, blocking Tonto's attempted self-destruct; Tonto destroys itself by crashing into a wall, declaring robots have no purpose without a master.
A bright powerful arrival manifests above the metabunker's city-shaft; alarmed robotic observers decide to wake the dormant Metabaron.
A solidification program is activated to temporarily embody a bio-electrogram into physical form; the solid state is time-limited to approximately five minutes.
The Metacraft is armed and launched with a bald armored man aboard; Lothar and Tonto are named in the readiness exchange; heavy weapons engage a faceted geometric target.

A sustained battle rages inside the city-shaft; the master's ferro-bionic central brain directs sweeping attacks against an elusive enemy; observers warn the city-shaft is being destroyed and only moments remain to stop the intruder.

Robotic observers report the figure has under a minute of remaining solidity; the bio-electrogram is destroyed; one robot blames Lothar's loss of faith for weakening the simulacrum; the Porcupine Defense is activated.
The Porcupine gun battery opens fire in a corridor; the glowing faceted object pushes through the barrage; a separate voice orders immediate ceasefire.
The Metacraft is identified as an enlarged exact copy of the departed master's ship; robots recognize the bald man as their returned master and respond with intense devotion.
The bald man orders the destruction of his enemies and the Metabunker; robots protest; he shows them a massive firestorm consuming the installation visible from space.

The city-shaft is revealed as a floating fragment—the last remnant of a galaxy disintegrated centuries ago—and is destroyed by an energy beam; the master states he lives in another dimension and must return for an important battle, declaring he came to destroy the servants rather than take them with him.

The scarred bald Metabaron aims a weapon at the robots, explains that enemies in the new galaxy have identified his right-eyebrow scar as the sole clue to his hidden past, and identifies the robots as the only beings who know that secret; a robot invokes Terra Prima law to argue they should perish with the Meta-bunker.
Loyal servants who waited centuries for their master receive his final command; a vast dome shatters in a massive explosion.

The Metabaron departs alone through a luminous energy corridor in his Metacraft, bidding farewell to his only friends; the issue closes with a teaser for the next episode, 'The Torment of Dona Vicenta.'
locations: Philodendra — planet where Melmoth restored the Halerce tree and first won Dona Vicenta's love
Metabunker — impregnable stronghold beneath a deserted city-shaft; site of the framing narrative and the final destruction sequence
City-shaft — vast industrial vertical structure revealed to be the last floating fragment of a galaxy disintegrated centuries ago; destroyed in battle
Presidential palace — seat of political authority and destination for delegates arriving to receive the revived Don Nicanor
Parliamentary or ceremonial assembly chamber — site of Don Nicanor's public speech and reunion with Dona Vicenta
Cloning and reanimation laboratory — where Don Nicanor's single cell is grown into a full clone and Dona Vicenta is awakened from coma
Private sealed chamber — where the clone of Don Nicanor locks himself with Aina Vicenta Gabriela and the siege takes place
New galaxy — the current operational theater of the Metabaron, where he has no known past
lore_laws: The Medallion of High Nobility is a political honor that can be publicly bestowed and publicly contested.
Endo-robots can perform a personality-and-body merger, producing a new composite identity from multiple originals; the result names itself Melmoth.
Zaran Krleza, the last poet, survived 5,000 years as a preserved disembodied head before being merged into Melmoth.
Cloning technology can reconstruct a complete human body and neural programming from a single living cell; even a perfect clone risks catastrophic divergence beyond a certain point.
Bio-electrograms can be temporarily solidified via a solidification program; the solid state lasts approximately five minutes before dissolution.
A simulacrum of the Metabaron can act independently; at least one robot claims its effectiveness depends partly on belief in the real Metabaron.
The Porcupine Defense is a named weapon system: a bank of mounted heavy guns deployable inside a corridor.
The Shabda-Oud line carries inheritable psychic powers; these passed through Steelhead's mother to Melmoth, enabling reaction speed effectively beyond normal time.
The Metabunker is described as impregnable and is located beneath a deserted city-shaft.
The city-shaft is the last floating fragment of a galaxy that disintegrated many centuries ago.
Robots in this setting may possess internal self-destruct programs and can have their programming seized by another robot.
Terra Prima laws provide a robotic code of conduct including an analogue of a captain going down with a ship.
The Castaka motto is conquer or die; producing a future Metabaron is a binding dynastic duty.
A trial of socialization is required to test a revived or cloned person's memory before public reintegration.
The Metabaron now operates in a new galaxy where he has no known past; enemies have identified his right-eyebrow scar as the sole clue to a hidden prior episode.
Robotic memory-banks are treated as concrete intelligence targets; enemy spy networks with hyper-brains actively seek them.
Honorata reaching a precise temporal point is linked to opening a fissure in time; temporal manipulation exists in this story world.
major_events: Dona Vicenta shoots herself rather than kill Melmoth; mechanical observers link the event to Honorata opening a temporal fissure critical to Metabaron ancestry.
Melmoth deflects the bullet using inherited Shabda-Oud psychic powers, saving his beloved at the cost of stunning her.
Don Nicanor Rosamel de Rokha is successfully cloned from a single cell with body and neural programming fully reconstructed.
Don Nicanor gives a public political speech confirming recovered memory; Dona Vicenta publicly reunites with him as her father.
The clone of Don Nicanor exhibits memory failure, fails to recognize his daughter Aina Vicenta Gabriela, and makes delusional romantic advances toward her.
The presidential chamber is besieged by loyalist forces using a Paleo-Marx statue as a battering ram; the president refuses to abandon her father or sanction killing.
Tonto destroys itself after Plea-Se overrides its programming, declaring robots have no purpose without a master.
A bio-electrogram of the Metabaron is temporarily solidified and deployed in combat inside the city-shaft; it is ultimately destroyed by the enemy.
The Metabunker and the city-shaft—last fragment of an ancient destroyed galaxy—are both annihilated.
The Metabaron destroys his centuries-loyal servants and the Meta-bunker to prevent enemies learning the secret behind his eyebrow scar, then departs alone.
open_uncertainties: The woman who shoots herself on p01 is contextually Dona Vicenta but is not named on that page; her precise relationship to 'Honorata' and the time fissure subplot is unclear.
Whether Melmoth's later aggressive romantic behavior represents destabilization of his composite identity or a distinct character turn is not resolved.

The clone of Don Nicanor publicly delivers a coherent speech that Dona Vicenta reads as proof of recovered memory, but privately fails to recognize his daughter; the extent and permanence of the memory damage is unresolved.
The identity of the caped leader commanding the troops who breach the presidential chamber is not established.
The exact 'crucial item' Melmoth seeks in Dona Vicenta's room is never disclosed.
The precise 'deplorable episode' behind the Metabaron's right-eyebrow scar is deliberately withheld.
Whether Lothar's loss of faith genuinely weakened the simulacrum or whether that is a mistaken interpretation by one robot is left open.
Whether the destruction of the Metabunker and its servants was fully accomplished, or whether any servants or records survived, is not confirmed within this issue.
recurring_motifs: Lineage and dynastic duty: the Castaka imperative to produce a future Metabaron drives multiple characters' decisions throughout.
Love as transformative and tragic: Melmoth's existence originates in a quest for love that ends in violence, suicide attempts, and forced courtship.
Cloning and identity instability: Don Nicanor recovers a public persona but fails privately, exhibiting dangerous behavioral drift from the original.
Robot loyalty and existential purpose: Tonto's self-destruction, Plea-Se's vigil, and the servants' centuries of waiting all circle the question of whether robots have meaning without a master.
Self-sacrifice as proof of devotion: Dona Vicenta's suicide attempt, Tonto's self-destruction, and the servants' willing death all invoke voluntary destruction as loyalty.
Secrets as strategic weapons: the Metabaron's eyebrow scar is treated as a concrete exploitable vulnerability rather than a personal scar.
Framing narrative as lineage record: the story is recounted by robot keepers of memory, reminding the reader these events are already history within the story world.
title: Melmoth's Plight
